sections.headline: Nvidia Earnings Boost S&P 500
sections.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.11% to 7348.35 as traders took a positive view of Nvidia's earnings report, which beat expectations. This move suggests investors are looking for signs of strength in the tech sector, which has been a key driver of the market's performance. [1]

sections.headline: Nasdaq Tech Stocks Rise Ahead of Nvidia Results
sections.body: Traders are watching Nvidia's earnings report, which is expected to impact tech stocks. Investors are also preparing for Anthropic's IPO, adding to the overall tech sector optimism. This sentiment boost led to a rise in Nasdaq futures and ultimately the Nasdaq index itself.

sections.headline: Yield Falls Amid Market Uncertainty
sections.body: The 10-year yield fell 0.76% to 5.06 as investors took a cautious approach to the market, citing concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on bond markets [8]. The move was also influenced by the recent slump in AI-related stocks, which may have led to a decrease in investor appetite for riskier assets [8]. Additionally, the warning from the Fed about a potential half-point rate hike may have contributed to the yield's decline, as investors sought to hedge against potential future interest rate increases [10].

sections.headline: USD/JPY Falls Amid Yen Buying
sections.body: The USD/JPY pair fell 0.12% to 159.33 as investors sought safe-haven assets amid a stock selloff and falling US yields. This move was driven by a surge in yen buying, which was sparked by concerns over potential Japanese intervention in the currency markets. Traders are watching the situation closely, with some analysts warning of a potential USD/JPY breakout support near 160.

sections.headline: Crude Oil Plunges Amid Supply Surplus Fears
sections.body: Crude oil fell 4.93% to 81.77 as traders worried about a supply surplus, despite recovering Middle East exports. The WSJ reported that higher US crude stocks and expectations of a supply surplus weighed on prices. Oil & Gas 360 also cited a larger US inventory build as a concern, reinforcing the downward trend.

sections.headline: Gold's Unexpected Drop
sections.body: Gold fell 3.15% to 3742.4 as traders reacted to rising expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, which is expected to increase the value of the US dollar and make gold less attractive. This move is also linked to lower demand for silver and gold coins, which is a sign of a weakening precious metals market. Traders are watching the Fed's next move closely to see if it will impact gold prices.

also.note: The Dow fell 400 points as Nvidia's earnings failed to soothe investors' nerves, according to the WSJ.
The Dow slid 400 points, with the Nasdaq seeing a seesaw effect as Nvidia's earnings bounced, according to CNBC.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were mixed, with Anthropic expected to price its IPO, according to MarketWatch.

S&P 500 (+0.11% to 7348.35): Nvidia Earnings Boost S&P 500. The S&P 500 rose 0.11% to 7348.35 as traders took a positive view of Nvidia's earnings report, which beat expectations. This move suggests investors are looking for signs of strength in the tech sector, which has been a key driver of the market's performance. [1]
Nasdaq (+0.77% to 24516.8): Nasdaq Tech Stocks Rise Ahead of Nvidia Results. Traders are watching Nvidia's earnings report, which is expected to impact tech stocks. Investors are also preparing for Anthropic's IPO, adding to the overall tech sector optimism. This sentiment boost led to a rise in Nasdaq futures and ultimately the Nasdaq index itself.
10-Year Yield (-0.76% to 5.06): Yield Falls Amid Market Uncertainty. The 10-year yield fell 0.76% to 5.06 as investors took a cautious approach to the market, citing concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on bond markets [8]. The move was also influenced by the recent slump in AI-related stocks, which may have led to a decrease in investor appetite for riskier assets [8]. Additionally, the warning from the Fed about a potential half-point rate hike may have contributed to the yield's decline, as investors sought to hedge against potential future interest rate increases [10].
USD/JPY (-0.12% to 159.33): USD/JPY Falls Amid Yen Buying. The USD/JPY pair fell 0.12% to 159.33 as investors sought safe-haven assets amid a stock selloff and falling US yields. This move was driven by a surge in yen buying, which was sparked by concerns over potential Japanese intervention in the currency markets. Traders are watching the situation closely, with some analysts warning of a potential USD/JPY breakout support near 160.
Crude Oil (-4.93% to 81.77): Crude Oil Plunges Amid Supply Surplus Fears. Crude oil fell 4.93% to 81.77 as traders worried about a supply surplus, despite recovering Middle East exports. The WSJ reported that higher US crude stocks and expectations of a supply surplus weighed on prices. Oil & Gas 360 also cited a larger US inventory build as a concern, reinforcing the downward trend.
Gold (-3.15% to 3742.4): Gold's Unexpected Drop. Gold fell 3.15% to 3742.4 as traders reacted to rising expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, which is expected to increase the value of the US dollar and make gold less attractive. This move is also linked to lower demand for silver and gold coins, which is a sign of a weakening precious metals market. Traders are watching the Fed's next move closely to see if it will impact gold prices.

- The Dow slid 400 points, with the Nasdaq seeing a seesaw effect as Nvidia's earnings bounced, according to CNBC.
- The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were mixed, with Anthropic expected to price its IPO, according to MarketWatch.

This growth is a positive sign for the industry, but traders are watching to see if it will continue. The growth in lumber prices is also being closely watched by companies in the forestry sector, who are looking for practical support to navigate the changing market. This is a key concern for companies like West Fraser, which is assessing the possibility of building a new sawmill in Scotland [38]. Meanwhile, in the fashion world, Timberland's iconic 6-inch boots are back in style, with a new color and luxe woven leather option. This is a positive sign for the company, but it's not directly related to the timber industry [40, 41].
